content: I'll read the test image and part index file to begin my analysis.

The test image shows green banana fruits (pods) with dark brown/black discoloration and shriveling at the tips (blossom ends). This is clearly a **pod** disease. Per the part index, pod candidates are: **Anthracnose** and **Cigar_End_Rot**.

I need to view all 7 classes first. Let me start with both pod candidates.
This Cigar_End_Rot reference shows dark shrunken tip on green banana - very similar to the test image! Now checking Anthracnose.

Anthracnose shows widespread dark spots on ripe yellow bananas - clearly different. The test image has green bananas with tip rot only. Now I need to cover all remaining 5 leaf classes with my remaining 5 views.

All 7 classes covered. The leaf diseases (Banana_Bunchy_Top_Virus, Bunchy_Top, Cordana_Leaf_Spot, Panama_Disease, Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka) clearly don't match the pod-focused test image. Now using my final view to confirm Cigar_End_Rot with a second reference.

This second Cigar_End_Rot reference is essentially identical to the test image — green banana bunch with dark, shrunken, necrotic tissue at the blossom ends of multiple fingers.

**Analysis Summary:**
- **Test image**: Green unripe banana bunch with dark brown/black dry rot confined to the blossom tips (distal ends) of multiple fingers
- **Plant part**: pod → narrows to Anthracnose or Cigar_End_Rot
- **Anthracnose** (PlantWild_26): scattered black spots across ripe *yellow* bananas — does not match
- **Cigar_End_Rot** (PlantWild_30, PlantWild_59): dark shrunken blossom-end rot on green bananas — matches perfectly in color, pattern, and location
- All leaf diseases (Sigatoka, Panama, Cordana, Bunchy Top, BBTV) are leaf-affecting and completely irrelevant
